question.text: In a resonance tube experiment, to determine the speed of sound in air, a pipe of diameter <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is used. The air column in the pipe resonates with a tuning fork of frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>480</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> when the minimum length of the air column is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>16</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. Find the speed of sound ( in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> ) in the air at room temperature.
